Name: Wave Grabbler (Public)
Source: Lyres Guide to Risk and Reward
Information:
A vehicle initially designed to be the city’s primary means of defense, but then adapted to be a recreational transportation vehicle for citizens who could afford them (or to be lent to organizations who would make use of them). They are, all at once, a military vehicle, a form of public transportation, and a heavy-duty labor implement. They use magnetic technology to adhere to metal surfaces and produce an instantaneous vacuum seal between themselves and surfaces they walk upon, allowing them to move across all dimensions without needing to adjust. This makes them incredibly useful when traveling across the walls separating the many Wards of the Rising Peak. Cables and arches are built between many areas specifically for these spider-like constructs to easily move across them.

Inside the back of the grabbler is enough space for about 10 regular-sized creatures across several layers oriented in a rotating fashion, similar to a rotating wheel that allows for separation and storage of its contents, accompanied by “walking space” below it.

Stat Blocks.title: Wave Grabbler (Public)
languages: understands Common and the languages of its creator, but doesn’t speak

traits.name: Headlights
traits.description: The construct can create a 30-foot-cone of bright light ahead of it, from which dim light extends an additional 30 feet. It can turn this light on or off at will on its turn.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Trample
actions.description: The construct moves up to half its movement speed in a straight line, trampling over any creatures in those spaces as it does. Each creature it enters the space of must succeed a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 13 (2d12) bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Medium-sized or smaller creatures who succeed this save (or would end their turn in the construct’s space) move into the nearest unoccupied space outside the construct’s path. If a Huge or larger creature succeeds their save, the construct stops moving immediately without entering their space. Creatures who fail are pushed into the nearest unoccupied space outside the construct’s path and fall prone.

reactions.name: Orientation Matrix
reactions.description: When the construct would take falling damage or fall prone, it can use its reaction to reduce the falling damage to half and/or immediately stand upright.
